narrative:
The decision regarding your law school application was influenced by a prediction that you have a 68% chance of failing the bar exam on your first attempt. This high probability indicates significant concerns about your preparedness for the exam, which ultimately led to the rejection of your application.

The most influential factor in this prediction was your performance in your third year of studies, where you ranked in the lowest decile compared to your peers. This suggests that your academic performance did not align with the expectations of successful bar exam candidates, as the average for accepted students was notably higher. Additionally, your LSAT score was considerably below the average of those who were admitted, further raising concerns about your readiness for the rigors of law school and the bar exam.

While your undergraduate GPA was slightly above average, it was not enough to offset the impact of your lower rankings in both your third-year performance and standardized testing. These two factors pushed the prediction toward a higher likelihood of failure, overshadowing your academic achievements.

Moving forward, it would be beneficial for you to focus on improving your academic performance and preparing for standardized tests. Consider seeking additional support or resources that can help enhance your study skills and test-taking strategies. Strengthening these areas could significantly improve your chances of success in future applications and on the bar exam.
